searchText: Hi Micah. A quick question about EIP1559: does `signature_y_parity` = `0x00` means `R.y` is odd or `R.y` is even? It is confusing for me as it is typed `bool` in the EIP1559, so I would expect `0x00` means `false` a.k.a odd, but this seems to contradict the old `v` parameter meaning (`v = y % 2`). `y_parity` is *not* the same as `v`. > `YParity` The parity (0 for even, 1 for odd) of the y-value of a secp256k1 signature. EIP-2930 has a better definition: <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2930#specification> Which is where it first appeared in the protocol. Ok, so it is not a boolean, because parity = true(1) means even It is a `bit`. 😄 The idea was to make code easy with `y % 2` instead of `!(y % 2)` or something. Ok, I get it. Thanks for the clarification! 🙂
